results.notes: Substrate mechanically confirmed: corpus segments for 1:1-1:4 contain zero 2nd-person features (all divine references 3rd-person/genitive epithets); the first 2MS is iyyaka (PRON|2MS) at 1:5, then na'budu/nasta'inu (1P IMPF), ihdina (2MS IMPV) at 1:6, an'amta (2MS PERF) at 1:7. Iltifat at 1:5 is classically grounded (al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn both dwell on iyyaka's exclusivity; the balaghah tradition treats it as the paradigm iltifat). Two problems force a hedge: (1) '1:4 is the exact center of seven' holds only in the Kufan/Hafs verse count where the basmala is verse 1 — in the Medinan/Basran counts the basmala is not numbered and the center shifts, so the arithmetic-center claim must be flagged as count-dependent. (2) Site consistency: content/tadabbur/001-al-fatiha/ayah-005.md already says the shift happens 'at the exact midpoint of the surah' and calls 1:5 'the hinge' of two halves (matching the hadith qudsi that splits the surah mid-1:5, 'half for Me, half for My servant'). The candidate's overlap note understates this — the new piece must position 1:4-as-pivot as a complementary modern structural reading (Islahi/Farrin lineage), not the discovery of an unnoticed seam.
results.corrected: Keep the reveal but reframe: the iltifat at 1:5 is the classical, universally-noted turn (al-Razi, al-Zamakhshari; the hadith qudsi splits the surah in the middle of 1:5 itself). The NEW observation — offered explicitly as a modern structural reading — is that in the standard Hafs numbering (seven verses counting the basmala), the verse of Judgment (1:4) sits at the arithmetic center, so the person-shift lands immediately after the surah's midpoint: description crescendos to accountability, and only then does address become possible. Flag the count-dependency in one honest sentence, and cross-link (not duplicate) the existing 1:5 tadabbur's hinge framing.

results.notes: Every substrate fact checks in the corpus: 108:1 opens with inna (ACC|FAM) + a'tayna (1P PERF VF:4) + -ka (2MS) + al-kawthar (ROOT:kthr); 108:2 opens fa+salli (2MS IMPV VF:2) + li-rabbi-ka (2MS) + inhar (2MS IMPV VF:1); 108:3 opens with inna + shani'a-ka (2MS) + al-abtar (ROOT:btr). So the inna/inna bracket, the single fa-imperative center, the 2MS kaf in all three verses, and the kthr/btr root antithesis at the two ends are all literal first-words/roots. Classical grounding for the polarity is solid: al-Muyassar glosses kawthar as al-khayr al-kathir; al-Jalalayn lists river/prophethood/Quran/intercession; abtar = cut off is the unanimous classical reading. The A-B-A' bookend framing itself is a modern reading and the candidate correctly flags it. Overlap: no published article covers al-Kawthar; tadabbur files (108/ayah-001.md, ayah-003.md) treat inna and abtar in depth at verse level but neither frames the three-verse bookend architecture — the article should lead with the structure rather than re-doing the inna exegesis.

Two independent grounds. (1) DUPLICATION: the reveal is already published on the site. content/tadabbur/097-al-qadr/ayah-004.md (line ~225) states: 'Surah Al-Qadr opens, in ayah 1, with the verb anzalnahu... here, in ayah 4, the surah's center, the verb is tanazzalu... The same root. N-z-l. The surah is bracketed by descent.' And 097-al-qadr/ayah-005.md (line ~293) already does the whole-surah shape (descent of revelation to rising of fajr). The candidate's overlap_note claimed 'None found' — false. (2) SUBSTRATE GEOMETRY: the individual corpus facts are true (97:1 anzalna 1P PERF VF:4 root nzl with -hu; 97:4 tanazzalu 3FS IMPF VF:5 root nzl; laylat al-qadr in vv.1-3; v3 is the arithmetic middle of five), but the framing claim 'the same root n-z-l opens and closes the surah, framing the center' is wrong: v5 (salamun hiya hatta matla' al-fajr) closes the surah with no nzl, and v1/v4 are not symmetric around v3 (the symmetric pairs of five are 1-5 and 2-4). The inclusio is imposed on the geometry even where the two descents are real.

The verifiable pairings are real: heavens+earth (ROOT:smw + ROOT:ard) occur in exactly two clauses of 2:255 ('lahu ma fi as-samawati wa ma fi al-ard' and 'wasi'a kursiyyuhu as-samawati wa al-ard' — no other occurrence); the sleep-denial ('la ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm', roots wsn/nwm) pairs with the fatigue-denial ('wa la ya'uduhu hifzuhuma', root awd); and there are exactly two illa-qualifiers ('illa bi-idhnihi', 'illa bima sha'a'). Overlap claim checks out: 002-al-baqarah/ayah-255.md presents the ten statements linearly with no ring, and the published throne-twin article is about an external echo verse. BUT the candidate misidentifies the center. Under the natural chiastic division (9 units: [1] la ilaha illa huwa al-Hayy al-Qayyum, [2] sinah/nawm, [3] lahu ma fi as-samawat wal-ard, [4] intercession illa bi-idhnihi, [5] ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum, [6] knowledge illa bima sha'a, [7] wasi'a kursiyyuhu as-samawat wal-ard, [8] la ya'uduhu hifzuhuma, [9] wa huwa al-'Aliyy al-'Azim), the symmetry is clean — 1<->9 transcendence, 2<->8 no-weakness, 3<->7 heavens+earth, 4<->6 the two illa-clauses — and the DEAD CENTER is [5], God's comprehensive knowledge, NOT the permission pair. The candidate's ten-clause layout with the two permission clauses at center breaks the very symmetry it invokes. Classical tafsir (Tabari, Jalalayn, Muyassar checked) expounds linearly and does not note the ring, so the geometry must carry an explicit modern-reading flag (the candidate does flag this).
results.corrected: Rebuild on the 9-unit chiasm: outer frame = transcendence (no god but He, the Ever-Living / the Most High, the Great); ring 2 = two denials of weakness (no drowsiness or sleep / preserving them never tires Him); ring 3 = the only two heavens-and-earth clauses (all in them is His / His Kursi spans them); ring 4 = the twin 'except' clauses (no intercession except by His leave / no grasp of His knowledge except as He wills); CENTER = 'He knows what is before them and what is behind them.' Retitle accordingly — the core of the greatest verse is His knowledge, wrapped by His permission, wrapped by His ownership, wrapped by His tirelessness, wrapped by His transcendence. Flag explicitly as a modern structural reading (Farrin; Neuwirth on ring form); the classical tradition reads the statements linearly.
